name: Metformin
aliases: Glucophage, Glucophage XR, Glumetza, Fortamet, Riomet, metformin hydrochloride, metformin ER, metformin XR, metformin SR, dimethylbiguanide
halfLife: About 6 h in the blood, about 18 h in red blood cells
summary: Metformin is the medicine most often prescribed for type 2 diabetes, and the first one tried for it. It lowers blood sugar by making the liver release less glucose and the body more sensitive to its own insulin, and on its own it seldom pushes blood sugar too low. It’s also prescribed for polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), to hold off diabetes in people at high risk, and for the weight gain antipsychotics can cause. It does nothing to mood or the mind: a dose isn’t felt.

pharmacology.text: How it works isn’t fully settled. In the liver it slows the making of new glucose, in part by acting on the cells’ mitochondria and switching on an enzyme called AMPK; in the gut it changes how sugar is taken up and raises the hormone GLP-1; and muscle takes up more glucose for the same insulin. It doesn’t make the pancreas release insulin, which is why it rarely causes low blood sugar by itself.

body.says: About 50–60% of a dose, less with food
About 6 h in the blood, about 18 h in red blood cells
Through the kidneys, unchanged, in urine

uses.text: Type 2 diabetes, on its own or with other medicines and insulin. It’s started low, at 500 mg once or twice a day with meals, and raised week by week to keep the stomach settled; blood sugar falls over the first days and the full effect takes about two weeks. It’s also used for polycystic ovary syndrome, where it can bring periods back and help with ovulation, for diabetes in pregnancy, to delay diabetes in people with prediabetes, and to limit the weight gain antipsychotics can cause. It has been studied for ageing and cancer, but there’s no proof it lengthens life in people without diabetes.
uses.brands: Glucophage, Glucophage XR, Glumetza, Fortamet, Riomet

sideEffects.text: Most side effects are in the gut: feeling sick, diarrhoea, stomach ache, wind and bloating, a metallic taste and a smaller appetite. They’re worst in the first weeks and after the dose goes up, and usually settle. Taking it with food, raising the dose slowly or changing to extended release helps. Some people lose a little weight on it.

advisory: Rarely, metformin builds up and causes lactic acidosis, which can kill. It’s most likely when the kidneys fail or the body is short of oxygen or water: severe dehydration, vomiting or diarrhoea that won’t stop, a serious infection, heart failure, heavy drinking, or an overdose. The signs are feeling very unwell with vomiting, stomach pain, muscle pain or cramps, fast deep breathing, feeling cold, a slow or uneven heartbeat, and drowsiness. Anyone who takes metformin and has these needs an ambulance.

warnings.text: Alcohol makes lactic acidosis more likely, and a lot of it, on an empty stomach, can drop blood sugar too, more so with other diabetes medicines. A drink or two with food is usually fine; a binge, or drinking day after day, is not. If you’ve been sick from drinking, skip metformin until you’re eating and drinking again.

When you’re ill with vomiting, diarrhoea, a fever or sweats, or can’t eat or drink, stop metformin and start again once you’ve been eating and drinking normally for 24 to 48 hours: it’s called the sick day rule. A long night dancing in the heat, on MDMA or another stimulant above all, dries the body out the same way, so eat, and sip water steadily, no more than about 500 mL an hour.

Metformin leaves the body only through the kidneys, so how much is safe depends on how well they work: the dose is lowered when kidney function (eGFR) falls below 45 and it’s stopped below 30. A blood test checks them before it’s started and at least once a year.

Before a CT scan or X-ray with an iodine contrast dye, an angiogram, or an operation under general anaesthetic, tell the team you take metformin. It’s often paused on the day and for 48 hours after, until a blood test shows the kidneys are fine.

Taken for years, metformin can lower vitamin B12. Too little B12 causes tiredness, anaemia, a sore tongue, and numbness or tingling in the hands and feet, so it’s worth a blood test every year or two, and sooner with any of these.

On its own metformin rarely causes low blood sugar. With insulin or a sulfonylurea such as gliclazide, after hard exercise, or after drinking without eating, it can: shaking, sweating, hunger, a racing heart and confusion. Eat or drink something sugary at once, then something starchy.

doseBasis: Amounts are for one dose, taken with or just after a meal. Immediate release is taken two or three times a day, up to 2,000 to 3,000 mg a day in all depending on the country (2,550 mg in the US); extended release once a day with the evening meal, usually up to 2,000 mg. Take it as it’s prescribed: more doesn’t do more that you’d notice, and a large overdose can cause lactic acidosis.

combinations.note: Alcohol makes lactic acidosis from metformin more likely, and a lot of it without food can drop blood sugar. A drink or two with a meal is usually fine: don’t binge, and skip metformin if you’ve been sick.
A long night on it, in the heat with little water, dries the body out and strains the kidneys, and metformin builds up when they slow. Eat, sip water steadily, and skip metformin if you’re vomiting.

fact.en: It comes from goat’s rue (French lilac), a plant used in medieval Europe for the thirst and frequent urination of diabetes. Its active compound, galegine, led chemists to the biguanides in the 1920s. Metformin reached France and Britain in the late 1950s but the US only in 1995.
fact.zh: 它源自山羊豆（法國丁香），這種植物在中世紀的歐洲被用來緩解糖尿病的口渴和頻尿。其中的活性成分山羊豆鹼，在 1920 年代引導化學家找到了雙胍類藥物。二甲雙胍在 1950 年代末就進入法國和英國，美國卻直到 1995 年才上市。
fact.zhHans: 它源自山羊豆（法国丁香），这种植物在中世纪的欧洲被用来缓解糖尿病的口渴和尿频。其中的活性成分山羊豆碱，在 1920 年代引导化学家找到了双胍类药物。二甲双胍在 1950 年代末就进入法国和英国，美国却直到 1995 年才上市。
